IncidentDef.label: a young beast from the herders

titles.li: A young beast from the herders

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a rider of {FACTION}, has come to the gate leading a young {TALE} on a rope of plaited hair. {X_nameDef} says the herders' elder chose it for {B_nameDef}: the herders believe that watching a beast graze shows whom it belongs with, and the elder watched this one. The colony can have it for {COUNT} silver, a fair price, or trade one of its own young beasts for it.

[ride] {X_nameDef}, a rider of {FACTION}, has come in leading a young {TALE} that is already used to a saddle. The elder at {PLACE} watched it graze for a season and decided it belonged with {B_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} asks {COUNT} silver, or one of the colony's young beasts in trade, and says it will carry {B_nameDef} anywhere.

[pack] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked a young {TALE} all the way from {PLACE}. It is a strong animal for carrying loads, with a halter of red wool. {X_nameDef} says their elder chose it for {B_nameDef}, and nobody argues with the elder about animals. The price is {COUNT} silver, or a young beast of the colony's own.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a rider of {FACTION}'s herders, has come to the gate barefoot beside a young {TALE}. "The grass will tell," {X_pronoun} says. That is what the elder said when this one kept wandering toward the colony's land, and the elder decided it belongs with {B_nameDef}, if the colony wants it. The price is {COUNT} silver, or a young beast in trade.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a rider of {FACTION} in a dusty coat, has come to the gate with a young {TALE} on a lead. {X_nameDef} says the herders still choose beasts the old way, and the elder chose this one for {B_nameDef}. The price is {COUNT} silver, or one of the colony's young beasts in trade.

[their:grateful] The herding folk remember the colony kindly, and their elder has sent {X_nameDef} with a young {TALE} chosen for {B_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} offers it at a friend's price of {COUNT} silver, or a young beast in trade.

li.label: Take the {TALE} for {B_nameDef} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, and {B_nameDef} is walking out to meet the young {TALE}.

li.label: Trade one of our own young beasts for it
li.outcome: One of the colony's young beasts is going back with {X_nameDef}, and {B_nameDef} is walking out to meet the {TALE}.

li.label: Thank the elder, but no
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} turns the young {TALE} round without a word of complaint and leads it back toward {PLACE}.

lines.li: [handed] The grass told the elder, and the elder told me.
[handed] Count it at dusk with the rest, and it will stay.
[handed] It knows you already, or it will by the evening.
[thanks] Another season, then, and maybe another beast.
[thanks] The grass is patient, and so are we.
[supper] A guest eats from the same pot, and this is a good pot.
[supper] We say the names of the herd before we eat, if you don't mind.

IncidentDef.label: a limb fitted by the order

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a surgeon of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a brother of the order carrying a long bag. The order heard that {B_nameDef} lost {B_possessive} {RELATION}, and has brought {TALE} to fit while {B_nameDef} lies in one of the colony's beds. They ask no silver. "We were spared, and so we owe," {X_nameDef} says. {B_nameDef}'s name would go into the Book of the Spared, the order's record of everyone it has healed.

[wooden] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a surgeon with a saw and a pot of glue on {X_possessive} belt, offers to fit {B_nameDef} with {TALE} for the {RELATION} {B_pronoun} lost, cut from the colony's own wood and shaped at the bedside. {X_nameDef} asks no silver, because the order believes it owes help to everyone it can mend.

[prosthetic] {X_nameDef}, a surgeon of {FACTION}, has brought {TALE}, wrapped in clean linen, from the order's sickhouse at {PLACE} to replace the {RELATION} {B_nameDef} lost. {X_nameDef} would fit it in one of the colony's beds, with the colony's doctor helping if the colony likes, and asks nothing for it.

[nodoctor] {X_nameDef}, a surgeon of {FACTION}, has come to the gate for {B_nameDef}, who lost {B_possessive} {RELATION}. The colony has nobody to assist at the bedside, so {X_nameDef} will work alone, fitting {TALE} in one of the colony's beds for no silver at all.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a surgeon of {FACTION}, has walked from {PLACE} with a peg-maker's tools and a lantern. {X_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} has been without {B_possessive} {RELATION} long enough, and offers to fit {TALE} in one of the colony's beds for nothing.

[their:grateful] The hospitallers remember the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} to repay it. {X_nameDef} offers to fit {TALE} for {B_nameDef}'s lost {RELATION} in one of the colony's beds, and asks no silver.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} fit it, {A_nameDef} at the bedside
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is going to lie down in one of the colony's beds, and {X_nameDef} is following with the order's tools. The colony owes the order for it.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} fit it, and send medicine back for their sickhouse
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is going to lie down for the fitting, and medicine is going out for the order's sickhouse, so the colony owes them nothing.

li.label: Not now
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} bows to {B_nameDef} at the gate and says the order's door is always open, then takes the road back to {PLACE}.

lines.li: [fit] Lie still, and let me see what the fall left you.
[fit] We were spared, and so we owe.
[thanks] The lamp is lit over our door for anyone, whenever.
[spared] Your name goes in the Book of the Spared tonight.
[spared] Walk on it gently for a week, and then walk on it however you like.
[sorry] I am sorry, it would not take, and I will say so in the book.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a storm reader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate soaked to the skin, with a glass vial on a cord around {X_possessive} neck. {X_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} has a better feel for storms than anyone at the colony. If they spent an hour out in this storm together, {B_nameDef} would come back with {TALE}. {X_nameDef} asks {COUNT} silver.

[rod] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} saw the colony's stormglass rod from the road and came straight in out of the thunderstorm. {X_nameDef} says that if {B_nameDef} stood at the rod with {X_objective} for an hour, {B_nameDef} would come back with {TALE}. The price is {COUNT} silver, or a vial of this storm caught at the colony's rod, for the Conclave's archive.

[tome] {X_nameDef}, a storm reader of {FACTION}, has come in out of the thunderstorm with a book wrapped in oilcloth under {X_possessive} arm. {X_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} has a feel for storms, and an hour out in this one together would teach {B_objective} what is written in the book: {TALE}. The price is {COUNT} silver.

[paths] {X_nameDef}, a storm reader of {FACTION}, has come to the gate while lightning flashes over the hills. {X_nameDef} says some of the Conclave can sense storms and some can command them, and {B_nameDef} could be one of those who command them. After an hour out in the storm with {X_objective}, {B_nameDef} would gain {TALE}. The price is {COUNT} silver.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a storm reader of {FACTION}, has come down the road in the thunderstorm with a copper-tipped staff. {X_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} has a feel for storms, and after an hour out in this one {B_nameDef} would come back with {TALE}. The price is {COUNT} silver.

[their:grateful] The Stormglass Conclave thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come in out of the storm to say that {B_nameDef} could learn to sense storms as they do. An hour out in it would give {B_nameDef} {TALE}, at a friend's price of {COUNT} silver.

li.label: Send {B_nameDef} out with {X_nameDef} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, and {B_nameDef} is walking out into the storm with {X_objective}.

li.label: Pay with a vial of our own storm, caught at our rod
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} are walking out to the colony's rod, and a vial of the colony's storm will go into the Conclave's archive.

li.label: Not in this weather
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} laughs, writes the date of the storm on {X_possessive} sleeve, and walks back out into it.

lines.li: [storm] Stand with your face up and count between the flash and the sound.
[storm] Never wrong, never sure, and never dry either.
[thanks] The glass says there will be other storms.
[woke] There, you heard that one before it came.
[woke] Now the storm knows your name as well.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a mech-tender of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a {TALE} walking behind {X_objective}. {X_nameDef} offers to install a mechlink in {B_nameDef}, which takes two hours and can be done wherever {B_nameDef} is standing, and to link the {TALE} to {B_objective} as a first mech. The price is {COUNT} silver, or two of the colony's basic subcores.

[subcores] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard the colony keeps subcores, and has come with a {TALE}. For two basic subcores or {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} would give {B_nameDef} a mechlink and the {TALE} to go with it.

[strange] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a woman in an indigo robe, has come up the path with a machine walking behind her. She offers to put a device called a mechlink into {B_nameDef}'s head, after which the machine would obey {B_nameDef}'s thoughts. She asks {COUNT} silver, or two of the small thinking cores the colony keeps, called subcores.

[!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a mech-tender of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a {TALE} and a case of tools. {X_nameDef} says the Lattice teaches others to control mechs, and {B_nameDef} has the aptitude for it. {X_nameDef} would install a mechlink wherever {B_nameDef} is standing and link the {TALE} to {B_objective} as a first mech, for {COUNT} silver or two basic subcores.

[their:grateful] The Lattice thinks well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has brought a {TALE} from {PLACE} for {B_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} would install a mechlink in {B_nameDef} and link the {TALE} to {B_objective}, at a friend's price of {COUNT} silver or two subcores.

li.label: Link {B_nameDef} ({COUNT} silver)
li.outcome: The silver is going out to {X_nameDef}, who is walking over to {B_nameDef} with the tools.

li.label: Pay with two basic subcores
li.outcome: Two subcores are going out to {X_nameDef}, who is walking over to {B_nameDef} with the tools.

li.label: No machines in our heads
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} nods, turns the {TALE} round with a thought, and the two of them go back to the road.

lines.li: [link] Keep still, it only tingles.
[link] A mind alone is a candle, and you are about to be less alone.
[thanks] The Lattice will be here if you change your mind.
[linked] Think of a load, and it will carry it.
[linked] There, you can hear it now, can't you.

titles.li: A tree seed from the Mossborn

texts.li: [tree] {X_nameDef}, a seed-carrier of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a seed the size of a fist wrapped in moss. The Mossborn keep a ledger of the trees each people fells and plants, and {X_nameDef} says the colony now stands well in it. The seed is meant for {B_nameDef}: it would be planted wherever the colony chooses, with {B_nameDef} helping, and the tree that grows would be bound to {B_objective}, along with its dryads in time. The price is a promise to plant a seedling for every tree the colony cuts down, and the Mossborn will check.

[tree,dryads] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has brought a {TALE} from the old grove at {PLACE}. The Mossborn believe every tree that is cut down should be replaced with a seedling, and the colony has done that, planting {COUNT} trees this season. The Mossborn have chosen {B_nameDef} to plant it with {X_nameDef}, wherever the colony chooses, and the tree and its dryads would be bound to {B_objective}.

[grove] {X_nameDef}, a seed-carrier of {FACTION}, has come with a pouch of {TALE} seed. The colony stands well in the Mossborn's ledger of trees felled and planted, and {X_nameDef} would sow a healroot grove wherever the colony chooses, with {B_nameDef} helping to learn how it is done. The only price is a promise to plant a seedling for every tree the colony cuts down.

[lowtech] {X_nameDef}, a seed-carrier of {FACTION}, has come out of the trees at the edge of the land with a seed in {X_possessive} hands. {X_nameDef} says the colony now stands well in the Mossborn's ledger of trees felled and planted, and the seed is meant for {B_nameDef}. The colony can plant it wherever it likes, if it promises to plant a seedling for every tree it cuts down.

[their:grateful] The Mossborn think well of the colony, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with a {TALE} for {B_nameDef}, to be planted wherever the colony chooses. They ask only their usual promise: a seedling planted for every tree cut down.

li.label: Plant it where we choose, and promise
li.outcome: The colony is choosing the spot, and {X_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} will plant it there together. The colony's promise is written in the Mossborn's ledger.

li.label: Let {X_nameDef} choose the spot, and promise
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} are walking the land to find a quiet spot away from walls. The colony's promise is written in the Mossborn's ledger.

li.label: No promises we can't keep
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} wraps the seed up again and says the Mossborn would rather hear an honest no than have a promise broken.

lines.li: [promise] A seedling for every tree, and the ledger watches.
[promise] Stand where I can see your feet, and we'll find the spot.
[thanks] The ledger stays open, and so does the grove.
[planted] There, now it knows your hand.
[planted] Talk to it in the evenings, it listens slowly.
[sown] Keep the weeds off it and it will keep the fever off you.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, a caravan master of {FACTION}, has stopped at the gate with {TALE}. The caravan can't carry it all, and the league would like to leave {COUNT} sealed crates in the colony's stores until a second caravan fetches them. {X_nameDef} would write the colony into the Waystone Book, the league's record of fair dealers, and the league would pay a tenth of what the crates hold as a fee when they are collected.

[beast] A caravan of {FACTION} has come slowly up the road behind a lame pack animal, and {X_nameDef}, its master, asks a favour: to keep {COUNT} sealed crates in the colony's stores until a second caravan comes for them. The league makes sure every crate reaches its owner, and these would get there by way of the colony.

[truck] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has walked up to the gate from a broken-down truck by the road. The league can't move the whole load, and asks the colony to keep {COUNT} sealed crates in its stores until a second truck fetches them. The fee is a tenth of what they hold.

[lander] {X_nameDef}, a factor of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a slate full of figures. {X_nameDef} says the league's lander is overloaded and would like to leave {COUNT} sealed crates in the colony's stores until it can fetch them. The league would pay a tenth of what they hold when they are collected, and write the colony into the Waystone Book as a fair dealer.

[their:grateful] The league counts the colony as a fair dealer, and {X_nameDef} would rather trust its crates to the colony than to anyone else on the road. {X_nameDef} asks the colony to keep {COUNT} sealed crates in its stores until a second caravan fetches them.

li.label: Keep them for the league's fee
li.outcome: {X_nameDef}'s porters are carrying the crates in to the colony's stores, and {X_nameDef} has opened the Waystone Book at a fresh page.

li.label: Keep them for nothing, as friends
li.outcome: The porters are carrying the crates in, and {X_nameDef} has written in the book that the colony kept them for nothing, as a friend.

li.label: We can't keep them
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} shrugs, says the road won't wait, and goes back to sort the load.

lines.li: [book] Good ink for you, and every crate counted.
[book] A word given at the waystone stands.
[thanks] The road won't wait, so neither will we.
[goodink] Every crate home, and your name in good ink.
[goodink] The book says you kept your word, and the book doesn't lie.
[redink] Red ink, and I'll be the one to write it.

IncidentDef.label: what lies in the old place

titles.li: What lies in the old place

texts.li: [walls] {X_nameDef}, a fellow of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with another member of the society and a cart of instruments. {X_nameDef} says they have read about {TALE} and would like to camp beside it and take measurements, then tell the colony exactly what is inside, whether something dangerous is sleeping there or nothing at all. They would leave what they learn to the colony for its own research.

[walls] Two scholars of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef} and a younger fellow, have come up the road arguing about a map. {X_nameDef} says nobody knows what is inside {TALE}. If the colony lets them camp beside it and take measurements, they will say what is inside before anyone opens it. If the colony would rather they took the risk, they will also open it themselves at the end.

[landmark] {X_nameDef}, a fellow of {FACTION}, has come to the gate with a surveyor's chain over one shoulder. {X_nameDef} says the society has only read about {TALE} on the colony's land, and two of them would like to camp beside it and measure it, and leave the colony everything they learn.

[lowtech] Two scholars of {FACTION}, {X_nameDef} and a younger one, have come to the gate with ink on their fingers and a wax tablet each. They would like to camp by {TALE} and measure it, then tell the colony what is inside, and leave their notes for the colony's researchers.

[their:grateful] The learned society remembers the colony kindly, and {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} to measure {TALE} for it. They would camp beside it, tell the colony exactly what is inside, and leave their notes for its research.

li.label: Let them measure it
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the other fellow are taking their cart out to {TALE} to make camp beside it.

li.label: Let them measure it, and open it themselves at the end
li.outcome: The scholars are taking their cart out to {TALE}. When they have measured it, they will break in, and whatever sleeps there will wake.

li.label: Leave it be
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} writes something long in the margin of the map and the two of them go back to the road.

lines.li: [measure] Nothing known should be lost, and nothing unknown should be opened blind.
[measure] Hold the chain straight, and don't step over the line.
[thanks] Strictly speaking, we only asked one question.

titles.li: A lantern at the edge of the land

texts.li: Lantern Wardens of {FACTION} are making camp at the edge of the colony's land, three of them and two hounds, because {BEAST} is on it. They will light the lantern every night and go out on its trail by day, and stay until it falls or the trail goes cold. They ask nothing yet, and say they will warn the colony when it comes near.

[legend] The Wardens of {FACTION} have hunted {BEAST} for years without catching it, and now that it is on the colony's land they have come to camp at the edge with their hounds and their lantern. They will follow its trail by day and keep the lantern lit by night, and the colony's best shot is welcome to join them.

[nemesis] {BEAST} is back on the colony's land, and Wardens of {FACTION} have come to camp at the edge of it. They hunt down any animal that has killed a person, and will stay until they have killed it or the trail goes cold.

[alpha] Wardens of {FACTION} have followed the pack that runs with {BEAST} onto the colony's land, and are making camp at its edge: three of them, two hounds and a lantern. They light their lantern where an animal has killed someone, and they mean to stay until the pack's alpha is dead.

[lowtech] Three Wardens of {FACTION} with boar-spears and two lean hounds are making camp at the edge of the colony's land, for {BEAST}. The lantern will burn all night at their fire, and they will be on its trail at first light.

[!lowtech] Wardens of {FACTION} have set up a post at the edge of the colony's land, with a lantern on a pole and two hounds on long leads. {BEAST} is out there, and they will track it by day and keep the lantern lit by night until it falls.

lines.li: [hunt] Keep behind the spears, and do not shoot past us.
[fell] Into the book with you, and the page closed.

IncidentDef.label: kill it or win it over

titles.li: Kill it or win it over

texts.li: Wardens of {FACTION} and a tamer of {ENEMY} have both come to the colony's gate for {BEAST} at the same time, and they are not speaking to each other. The Wardens want to hunt it, keeping its hide as a trophy and giving its meat to the colony. The tamer wants to tame it instead. The colony can side with one of them, or let them settle it in a bout at the gate.

[legend] {BEAST} is famous across the region, and both the Wardens of {FACTION} and a tamer of {ENEMY} have come for it. {X_nameDef} wants it dead, and the tamer wants it alive and bonded. Neither will hunt or tame it on the colony's land without the colony's permission, and both are waiting at the gate.

[alpha] {X_nameDef} of the Wardens and a tamer of {ENEMY} have both followed the pack that runs with {BEAST} to the colony's land. The Wardens want to kill the pack's alpha, and the tamer says a tamed alpha is worth far more than its hide. They ask the colony to choose, or to let them settle it themselves in a bout at the gate.

[pokemon] The Circuit's tamer has come for {BEAST}, a creature the Circuit has only heard of, and the Wardens of {FACTION} have come to hunt it before it hurts anyone. They are standing at opposite ends of the colony's gate, waiting for its word.

[lowtech] Two parties have come up the road for {BEAST}: Wardens of {FACTION} with spears and a lantern, and a tamer of {ENEMY} with a pouch of treats and a coil of rope. Each says the other will get someone killed. The colony may side with either, or let them have it out at the gate.

li.label: Side with the hunt, {A_nameDef} with the Wardens
li.outcome: The Wardens and {A_nameDef} have gone after {BEAST}, and the tamer has left the gate without a word.

li.label: Side with the taming, {B_nameDef} with the tamer
li.outcome: {BEAST} is marked for taming, and {B_nameDef} will try to win it over with the tamer beside {B_objective}. The Wardens have gone home.

li.label: Let them settle it in a bout at the gate
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} and the tamer are squaring up at the gate. Whoever wins has the beast; the colony stays out of it.

lines.li: [hunt] Its page has been open long enough.
[hunt,legend] Eleven years Garrow waited, and we will not wait that long for this one.
[tame] A bond is not a leash, and I'll show you what I mean.
[tame] Bring it something it likes, and come slowly.
[bout] First to the ground gives up the beast.
[wardenwon] The book gets its page.
[tamerwon] A bond is not a leash, and a spear is not a reason.
[tamed] There, it chose you, and that is the only way it works.
[wonover] Steady now, we're going home.
[fell] Into the book with you, and the page closed.
[fell] Good meat for the colony, and a good hide for the book.
